title: Boomerangs: Magic Sticks of Physics
summary: Josh and Chuck explain the boomerang: its history from hunting sticks (non-returning "rabbit sticks") to returning boomerangs, possibly invented by Aboriginal Australians, and the physics behind how a returning boomerang flies. Covered airfoil lift, the boomerang as a two-bladed propeller with an invisible axis, gyroscopic precession, the effect of wind and throw angle, safety, and a tutorial on how to throw one. The episode closes with listener mail from a nuclear plant worker correcting the show's earlier claim about fission and fusion and the strong nuclear force.

segments.title: Opening banter and boomerang overview
segments.summary: Hosts open with off-topic banter, then introduce boomerangs, distinguishing non-returning hunting sticks from returning boomerangs and noting the Australian association.

segments.title: Boomerang history and origins
segments.summary: The hosts discuss theories that boomerangs evolved from throwing sticks used in hunting, the oldest non-returning boomerang found in Poland, and Aboriginal Australians possibly using returning boomerangs for sport and for hunting birds with nets.

segments.title: Design of returning boomerangs
segments.summary: The hosts explain that returning boomerangs are lighter and more aerodynamic, are thrown vertically, and must be made for the thrower's handedness, with mirror-image left-handed versions.

segments.title: Physics: airfoil lift and gyroscopic precession
segments.summary: Chuck explains the wings as airfoils creating lift, the boomerang as two wings forming an invisible-axis propeller, and how spin plus linear momentum produce gyroscopic precession that turns the boomerang into an arc back to the thrower. Spin rate depends on wing length, angle, and throw force.

segments.title: Boomerang designs, turbulators, and balancing
segments.summary: The hosts describe boomerang designs with more wings, turbulators that add lift, battle boomerangs, and the difficulty of mass-producing handcrafted boomerangs, comparing the balancing to tire alignment.

segments.title: How to throw a boomerang and wind
segments.summary: The hosts cover the forces acting on a boomerang, the role of wind and angle of attack, safety warnings about losing sight of a thrown boomerang, and the proper pinch grip, wrist snap, and clap-catch technique.

segments.title: Wrap-up and sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts summarize the six-axis spin, mention sources, and direct listeners to the website and social channels.
